doc: The Spy in the Guildhall (slug guildhall-spy) - slot 5 of the master-everyday-2 batch (THR-1757).
Brief: `Docs/plans/encounters/master-everyday-2-brief.md`.
Revised packet: `Docs/plans/encounters/guildhall-spy-revised.md` (draft: `guildhall-spy-draft.md`).
plotHookRolled: hook.stranger_bargain, hook.stronghold_mobilization, hook.assassination_succeeded
plotHookTaken:  hook.stranger_bargain - a stranger is asked to clean the council's house, and the price
is a place inside it. Mobilization survives as the vote to close the gates.
Seed dice: p3 opportunity - opposition own_trait (True, Bitter) - disposition neutral -
agentRole judge_asked_to_rule - scale region - system conditions (advisory, not taken).
--- The narrator's 12 questions, answered ---
1 P1 arrival?      Yes: {actor} is at an inn in {location} where the councillors drink; {cast:warden} sits down.
2 P2 events?       The council votes at the next bell on closing the gates; one councillor is the rival city's spy.
3 P3 one stake?    Opportunity (rolled): whoever names the spy, quietly, is taken in by the Merchant Consortium.
4 <=80 words?      73 / 80 (opening + step-0 spine).
5 Read aloud?      Report throughout; no interior sensation.
6 Stated?          The vote, the spy, the quiet ask and the prize each take one plain sentence.
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? The keeper of the minutes and the letters are revealed only behind the test.
9 One named person? {cast:warden}; the spy, the councillors and the watch are role nouns.
10 Stake in a sentence? Can {actor} name the spy before the bell without the council knowing?
11 Cards verb+noun? Send A Guilty Dream, Show An Honest Face.
12 Opening per class? urban, written.
--- Mechanical design block ---
Crux            A rival city has an agent on the town council, and the guildhall's warden asks {actor} to
name the spy quietly before the vote.
Shape           Single Test. shadow 0.78 (fail_action). Linear, branch count 0. Mean 0.78, window fit 0.92.
Consequence hand (binding): story_seed + membership, no swap. Both on step success:
membership - membership_change join merchant_consortium ($actor, chronicle): the guild that
keeps the guildhall takes in the one who found its spy.
story_seed - placeless encounter_seed query #consortium_errand, delay 48: the council's quiet
gratitude comes back as Consortium work. Same side as the join, so the errand's premise
(the Consortium sent them) is true when it ripens (prose rule 7).
Standing        reputation_with $here -0.06 on step failure (backs the failure and critical_failure chips).
Opposition      The mortal's own trait, read from the graph: True (trait.core.core_integrity.virtue, -0.05,
unlocks the trait card Show An Honest Face) and Bitter (trait.core.core_hope.vice, -0.05).
False (trait.core.core_integrity.vice, +0.05) is the one variant for.
Cost channels   Whisper at essence 2; trait card at cost 0. No Heavy Hand, no rider, no darkness Undertow.
Cool failure    Nobody is killed, jailed or branded. The vote goes the rival city's way and the town that
sent for a master did not get one; at critical failure the master calls an honest councillor
a traitor in open hall - the name before the purse.
Reactions       Success side only: name the spy in open hall (reputation_with $here +0.03, bond_change
$cast:warden -0.10) or keep the name inside the council (bond_change $cast:warden +0.10).
Systems         cast, seeds, factions, reputation = 4.
Accepted limits No band-keyed step write: success_at_cost takes the same join + seed as success; its cost
is prose only. A mortal already on the Consortium's rolls gets no new membership
(already_member). The #consortium_errand query keeps the family eligibility filter, so the
errand withers outside a town, city or capital; the chip claims only that word reaches
the Consortium.
Expert collision Shadow on the board: find the coiners (master), raid a tithe barn, crack a strongroom
(experts). This verb unmasks a person and takes nothing.

template.name: The Spy in the Guildhall

openings.urban: {actor} is at an inn in {location} where the town councillors drink before each sitting. {cast:warden}, warden of the guildhall, sits down at their table.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
The council votes at the next bell on closing the gates to a rival city's trade. One of the councillors is that city's spy.

{cast:warden} asks {actor} to name the spy before the bell, and to do it without the council knowing. The Merchant Consortium will take in whoever does it.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: The spy is the councillor who keeps the minutes. {actor} found the rival city's letters sewn into the minute book's cover and gave them to {cast:warden} before the bell.
steps.successAfterimage: The spy is the councillor who keeps the minutes. {actor} matched the hand in the minutes to a letter bound for the rival city.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: {actor} named the keeper of the minutes before the bell, but asked too many councillors on the way. The spy heard of it and fled the town.
steps.failureAfterimage: {actor} still had no proof when the bell rang. The spy took a seat in the hall and voted.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: {actor} named the wrong councillor before the whole hall. The real spy sat quiet and voted with the rest.

effects.seedLabel: Word of the spy reaches the Merchant Consortium, which has work for {actor}.

nudges.name: Send A Guilty Dream
nudges.effectLine: Fill one sleeper's night with being found out, so they wake afraid and show it.

bandProse.critical_success: The keeper of the minutes woke the inn in the night, shouting the rival city's name.
bandProse.success: The keeper of the minutes came down pale at dawn and would not meet {actor}'s eye.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The keeper of the minutes woke from the dream and was packing before dawn.
bandProse.near_miss: Half the council slept badly that night, and every one of them looked guilty at dawn.
bandProse.failure: The dream fell on an honest councillor, who told the whole inn about it at breakfast.
bandProse.critical_failure: The dream fell on an honest councillor, and {actor} took the councillor's fear for guilt.

nudges.name: Show An Honest Face
nudges.effectLine: Let their plain dealing disarm suspicion, so the guilty answer them without guarding their words.

bandProse.success: {actor} asked every councillor straight out, and the keeper of the minutes was the only one who lied.
bandProse.failure: {actor} asked straight out, and the councillors took offence and stopped talking.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being True, they cannot hide what they are asking about.
Being Bitter, they suspect every councillor alike.
Being False, they lie to the council as easily as the spy.
